mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from zero during high-rate regimes (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (indirectly reflected via UNRATE) signals weak labor market recovery, which suppresses equity risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: During similar labor weakening events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% monthly for two consecutive months predicts excess demand for capital goods, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 30 similar acceleration events, less than 40% produce positive 5-day forward returns (K-uplift p > 0.6).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for 4 consecutive months indicates a cooling demand environment that reduces policy rate uncertainty, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: In deflationary regimes, 20-day forward returns show no mean reversion (AR(1) p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-week moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, it signals a shift toward accommodative policy, which amplifies equity valuation multiples and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: 6-week moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%
failure_condition: During prior 6-week FEDFUNDS declines below 4%, 20-day forward returns failed to beat the risk-free rate (Sharpe ratio < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in unemployment (PAYEMS) and rise in consumer confidence (not directly observable but implied by labor market strength) creates a dual signal of job market improvement, which reduces equity risk aversion and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In analogous labor market strengthening events, 20-day returns show no statistically significant improvement (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) followed by a sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) within the same month suggests supply-side imbalance that elevates growth expectations and drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >1% in a month while INDPRO rises by >4% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 50 such co-moving events, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (Granger causality p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 5%), the compression of corporate discount rates through higher policy rates consistently produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In >10 similar tightening regimes, 20-day forward returns average positive or zero (mean p-value > 0.5).
